A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CineTrans/Cine250K work and contain readable methods, equations, results, figures, and appendices. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation benchmarks, component ablations, attention analyses, shot-segmentation measurements, and a user study.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds experiments on additional backbones, soft masking, and ambiguous shot boundaries.

M1.justification: The core block-diagonal mask, Visible-First-Frame attention, multi-prompt mechanism, and fine-tuning procedure remain unchanged. v2 Appendix D.5 adds optional Gaussian frame-distance and diffusion-timestep-dependent soft masks that permit cross-shot interactions. These extend the procedure while retaining hard masking as the primary method.

E1.justification: Cine250K and the 100-prompt, four-category evaluation remain. v2 additionally tests smoother/deformation and fade transitions and overlapping or ambiguous shot boundaries, extending transition requirements and input conditions within the existing multi-shot task.

E2.justification: The quantitative benchmark and user-study comparator sets are unchanged. However, Figure 5 omits StoryDiffusion+CogVideoXI2V from the sunset comparison and Wanx2.1-T2V-turbo from the traveler comparison, where both appeared in v1. This reduces the displayed per-example comparisons; VideoCrafter2 and Wan2.2 serve as additional experimental backbones.

E3.justification: The original training budgets, evaluation prompts, and metrics remain. v2 substantially expands experimental design through controlled transition-versus-camera-motion cases, layer-selection tests on additional backbones, Gaussian-width and denoising-schedule sweeps, and boundary perturbations of plus/minus one or two temporal slices. These are protocols for added experiments.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's masking, fine-tuning, and layer-position analyses, v2 adds quantitative layer-transfer tests on VideoCrafter2/Wan2.2, camera-motion controls, soft-mask sensitivity, extreme shot-length examples, and ambiguous-boundary robustness tests. It also replaces the illustrated failure case. These substantially broaden the questions investigated.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix D.1 newly specifies that the transition-versus-camera-motion examples use different seeds with other conditions held fixed. This is limited additional seed information. Existing confidence-interval plots, Pearson testing, and user-study uncertainty reporting remain; no increased repeated-run budget is documented.

E6.justification: The principal benchmark, original ablation, and user-study numbers are unchanged. v2 Tables 6–8 and 10–12 add substantial attention, backbone, soft-mask, and boundary-perturbation results. For trained CineTrans-DiT, transition control is 0.5193 with sigma=L/12 and 0.5461 with one-slice boundary jitter, versus the retained fixed hard-mask value of 0.7003. These are results under additional conditions.

T1.justification: v2 Equation 8 introduces the Gaussian frame-distance soft-mask definition. The original attention and masking definitions remain, while transition-score and Jensen–Shannon-distance formulas are relocated or algebraically combined. No new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: Cine250K, attention-guided masking for coherent controlled multi-shot generation, training-free transfer, and specialized evaluation metrics. The added investigations do not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations of smoothness/control/diversity tradeoffs, layer-selection transfer, and robustness to ambiguous boundaries. Appendix F shifts the illustrated failure from character inconsistency to overly similar compositions and adds limitations concerning detailed scene/background annotations. Section 5.2 also strengthens the control description to 'near-perfect' despite unchanged benchmark scores.

D1.justification: v2 discloses random selection among predefined transition points and specifies 20 user-study prompts with ratings from 1 to 5. It also states that code accompanies supplementary material and describes script-based Vimeo access without raw-video redistribution. These add documentation and access information without establishing changes to the retained experiments.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds substantive discussions of temporal control and masked attention, citing works including VSTAR, DiTCtrl, FlexiFilm, BEiT, MaskGIT, and VideoMAE. It explicitly positions CineTrans within existing attention-control research and distinguishes shot-level transitions from frame-level evolution, substantially broadening v1's research positioning.

P1.justification: Retained prose receives localized tightening and cross-reference corrections. Problem Formulation becomes a methodology preliminary subsection; metric formulas move into the main text, while dataset comparison and user-study material move to appendices. Ethics, reproducibility, and LLM-use statements are added, but much of the original narrative remains.

P2.justification: Figure 5 is redesigned from full-page sequence rows into compact side-by-side comparisons, and Figure 6 shows fewer frames. Dataset and user-study tables are relocated. Numerous new attention, distribution, soft-mask, and robustness displays are added, and the failure illustration is replaced, substantially changing the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The added backbone tests and camera-motion contrast strengthen validation of the masking rationale, while soft-mask and boundary-jitter experiments expose useful tradeoffs. Additional procedural and limitation details improve assessability. These gains are tempered by the new 'near-perfect' control wording and inconsistent attention-ratio labels in Tables 6–7, yielding a modest net improvement.
